newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa maize harvest slow despite drier weather.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa maize harvest slow despite drier weather.

text.p: Harvesting of South Africa's 1997 maize crop has started again after dry weather in the past week, but the pace is very slow as plant moisture content remains high, the producers body said on Thursday.
The annual harvest, which usually starts in May, has been delayed by over a month following unseasonal wet weather, raising fears that traders may have problems meeting export commitments.

"Harvesting is taking place but very slowly. It seems it will take some time yet for the crop to be fully harvested," Giel van Zyl, general manager of the National Maize Producers Organisation told Reuters.
"Very little has been harvested, I would say in the vicinity of 20 percent maybe," adding that in a normal year considerably more would have been harvested by this time.
Van Zyl said the worst-hit area was the eastern Mpumalanga province, where fields were still too wet for farmers to deploy machinery.
"In other areas where they can get into the fields the maize's moisture content is too high. You cannot deliver maize with a moisture content of above 16 percent."

He said the slow harvest meant it was impossible to give an accurate forecast of the 1997 crop. In view of this the National Crop Estimates Committee on Monday left its monthly commercial estimate unchanged at the May level of 7.660 million tonnes.

The committee said the wet weather was having an adverse effect on the quality of maize. This year's estimate is one to two million tonnes above consumption, but well below last year's 9.694 million tonnes.
